chunks: And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from some of our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

A man entered into a mukātabah contract with his slave and stipulated against him that his inheritance would belong to him. So that was referred to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, and he invalidated his condition and said: "The condition of Allah comes before your condition."

key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: Imam ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام in his role as legal authority and judge.
key_terms.شَرْطُ اللَّهِ: The divine legal condition or ruling set by Allah.
key_terms.فَأَبْطَلَ شَرْطَهُ: He ruled the stipulation invalid and without legal effect.
key_terms.كَاتَبَ مَمْلُوكَهُ: He entered into a mukātabah contract of manumission with his slave.
key_terms.مِيرَاثَهُ: His inheritance or estate after death.

ai.seo_question: Can a master stipulate ownership of a mukātab slave’s inheritance in a mukātabah contract?
ai.summary: This hadith states that when a master made a mukātabah agreement with his slave and added a condition that the slave’s inheritance would revert to him, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام nullified that stipulation. It establishes that private contractual conditions are invalid when they conflict with the ruling set by Allah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5741 - In the narration of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from some of our companions from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as):

"A man entered into a kitabah (contract of manumission) with his slave and stipulated that the slave's inheritance would belong to him. This matter was presented to the Commander of the Faithful (as), who invalidated the condition and said:
'The condition of Allah (swt) takes precedence over your condition.'"
